SEC Charges Investment Adviser with Misleading Investors About Fees

Published 2026-10-07 12:30 UTC

The Securities and Exchange Commission today charged a registered investment adviser with misleading clients about the fees it charged, resulting in overbilling of approximately $12 million over five years.

According to the SEC's order, the adviser told clients in its disclosure documents that advisory fees would be calculated based on the value of assets at the end of each quarter. In practice, the firm calculated fees using the highest value of the assets during the quarter, which inflated the fees paid by more than 3,000 clients, many of them retirees.

The order also finds that the adviser failed to disclose that it received payments from mutual fund companies for recommending certain share classes, which created a conflict of interest. Clients were placed in more expensive share classes when cheaper versions of the same funds were available.

The SEC's order finds that the adviser violated the antifraud provisions of the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 and the compliance rule. Without admitting or denying the findings, the adviser agreed to a cease-and-desist order, a censure, and to pay disgorgement and prejudgment interest totaling $13.4 million, which will be distributed to harmed clients, along with a civil penalty of $2.5 million.

The firm also agreed to retain an independent compliance consultant to review its fee billing practices and disclosures. The SEC's investigation was conducted by the Division of Enforcement's Asset Management Unit.

Investors who believe they may have been overbilled by an adviser can submit a tip or complaint through the SEC's website. The SEC encourages investors to review their account statements carefully and to ask their advisers to explain how fees are calculated.

The SEC reminds advisers that fee calculations must match the methods described to clients, and that conflicts of interest arising from third-party compensation must be fully and fairly disclosed. The Division of Examinations has identified fee billing as a continuing area of focus in its annual priorities.
